candidates.exact_span: Stream segment specific (20.6.4.401 NMAC) WQS for pH, 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (s.u.), are more restrictive than the technology-based limits presented earlier and downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for pH (i.e., 5-9 s.u. for domestic water supply, 6.5-9 s.u. for agricultural water supply, etc.). The pH limits of 6.6 to 9.0 s.u. in the previous permit, which are protective of the downstream Navajo Nation standards, will be continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the numeric pH discharge limit (6.6–9.0 s.u.) and states it will be continued; a different reading of whether these draft-continued limits are the operative enforceable limits for FY2025 would change which limit is compared against reported pH measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Regulations promulgated at 40 CFR §122.44(d) require limits in addition to, or more stringent than effluent limitation guidelines (technology based). NM WQS that are more stringent than effluent limitation guideline and applicable for this discharge are based on 20.6.4 NMAC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frames which limits are enforceable permit limits (WQS-based, more stringent than technology-based guidelines); interpreting applicability of 20.6.4 NMAC WQS versus technology-based limits would change which numeric limit governs compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: Primary contact currently is one of the designated uses of State of New Mexico Segment No. 20.6.4.401 of the San Juan basin. The State of New Mexico WQS criteria applicable to the primary contact designated use of the receiving stream are the monthly geometric mean of E. coli bacteria of 126 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL) and single sample of 410 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies state WQS numeric E. coli criteria (126 geometric mean; 410 single sample) tied to the primary contact designated use; whether these state criteria or the separately stated permit limits govern would change the applicable numeric thresholds for compliance.

candidates.exact_span: The results for E. coli may be reported as either colony forming units (CFU) or the most probable number (MPN) depending on the analytical method used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates CFU and MPN are interchangeable reporting units for E. coli; interpreting whether reported values in one unit are directly comparable to limits expressed in either unit could change exceedance determinations.

candidates.locator: page 9, fact_sheet, section 5.b (Bacteria, TMDL mass loading)
candidates.exact_span:
The E. coli daily mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the TMDL was established based on the following:

Daily mass loading limit, cfu/day = C, cfu/100 mL * 1,000 mL/L * l/0.264 gallons * Q, flow, expressed in 1,000,000 gallons/day

Where:
C = state water quality standard criterion for bacteria, 126 cfu/100 mL
Q = stream flow in million gallons per day (mgd), 299 MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: States a numeric daily mass loading limit (3.19 x 10^10 cfu/day) and its derivation inputs (C=126, Q=299 MGD); different interpretation of whether this mass-loading limit is enforceable or how it is calculated from reported data would change limit applicability and exceedance analysis.

candidates.exact_span: Downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for E. coli bacteria are 126 cfu/100 mL monthly geometric mean for domestic water supply, and 235 cfu/100 mL to 575 cfu/100 mL single sample maximum for secondary human contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides downstream Navajo Nation numeric E. coli criteria (126 geometric mean; 235–575 single-sample range) cited as basis for permit limit selection; interpreting which downstream standard is controlling could change the applicable single-sample numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monthly geometric mean limit of 126 cfu/100 mL, daily maximum limit of 235 cfu/100 mL and daily maximum mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the previous permit will be continued in the draft permit to be consistent with the New Mexico TMDL and protective of the more stringent NNWQS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicitly lists three enforceable numeric E. coli limits to be continued (geometric mean, daily maximum concentration, daily mass loading); whether these continued draft limits are operative for FY2025, and whether the 235 cfu/100 mL daily maximum supersedes the 410 cfu/100 mL state single-sample criterion stated earlier, would change compliance computations.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monitoring frequency requirement in the previous permit be also continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that an E. coli monitoring frequency requirement will be continued by reference to the previous permit without restating the frequency here; interpreting what frequency obligation carries forward would change which monitoring events were required during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monitoring frequency requirement in the previous permit be also continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: For monitoring periods lacking reported E. coli results, whether a frequency requirement was in effect (via continuation from the previous permit) affects whether missing data reflects a documented no-requirement state, inadequate evidence of required monitoring, or an unresolved case.
